record.title: Onboarding folder exposed
record.summary: At 09:41 a driver rang the depot: a search engine result for their own name led to our 'Driver onboarding' folder on the Fleet SharePoint site. The folder holds right-to-work scans, passport and licence photos and proof-of-address letters for 212 agency drivers (1,906 files). Its sharing was set to 'Anyone with the link'. First questions: who created the link and when, who used it without signing in, whether anything was downloaded, and what the search engine cached. Personal data, so the UK GDPR clock is running until we've assessed the risk.

with.summary: A sharing link on the 'Driver onboarding' folder let anyone with the link open right-to-work scans, passport and licence photos for 212 agency drivers, for 41 days (#{f_leak}). The fleet coordinator made it to send the folder to the driver agency (#{f_who}). with.recommendation: Keep the audit retention at 180 days or more on the E5 licences.

record.title: Kerberoasting
record.summary: Hypothesis: an intruder with a foothold is requesting RC4 service tickets for accounts with SPNs, to crack their passwords offline (T1558.003). Why now: Intelligence reports the Helix affiliate roasting service accounts within a day of initial access, and 14 of our SPN accounts still accept RC4. Look for 4769 events with ticket encryption 0x17 from workstations, outside the backup window, against more than five SPNs in a few minutes. Disproved by: no such bursts in 30 days of 4769 from all four DCs, beyond the vulnerability scanner's known pattern.

keys.kh1: Choose data sources and time range
keys.kh4: Conclude: promote it, close it, or refine the hypothesis
keys.kh5: Write up the detection for Shikari's library
keys.kh6: Share what was found with Intelligence

steps.body: Data sources: 4769 from all four DCs is in Sentinel for 90 days. One gap: DC03 stopped forwarding for six hours on the 2nd, so anything in that window would be invisible. record.title: Finance ransomware
record.summary: Defender XDR alerted at 07:31 on mass renames to .hlx on FS01 and FS02. A ransom note (HOW_TO_RESTORE.txt) in every folder names a leak site and gives ten days. The payroll and freight-planning shares are encrypted; FS03 (HR) shows an attempted launch. FIN-WS-0142, the source in the Kerberoasting hunt, connected to both servers just before encryption. Priorities: contain, keep payroll running for Friday, establish whether data left before encryption, and start the ICO and insurer clocks. record.title: Supplier invoice fraud
record.summary: Accounts payable reported an email from a known haulage supplier asking to change bank details for invoice INV-88412 (£48,210), due in Friday's payment run. The request came from the supplier's real mailbox, which looks compromised, and an inbox rule in our AP clerk's mailbox was hiding the supplier's replies. Payment is on hold. Scope: how the clerk's account was taken over, what was sent from it, whether other suppliers or users were targeted, and whether any money moved.

keys.kb0: Pull the reported message and its headers
keys.kb3: Check for credential entry and sign-ins
keys.kb4: Inspect mailbox rules, forwarding and app consents
keys.kb6: Check for payment or data requests

Registered three days ago; replies were redirected here.

with.summary: A haulage supplier's compromised mailbox asked us to change bank details for INV-88412 (£48,210). Our AP clerk's account had been taken over the night before by MFA fatigue from a scripted client (#{f_signin}); an inbox rule hid the supplier's replies (#{f_rule}), and the attacker sent phishing to two more suppliers from the clerk's mailbox (#{f_sent}). The VPN was not used (#{f_vpn}, refuted). No payment was made (#{f_pay}). The rule is gone, sessions are revoked, number matching is on for every account, and the bank has flagged the payee. Whether other finance users were targeted is with #{consent}.

Money at risk and money moved

with.observation: Push approval without number matching let a scripted client through after a handful of prompts.
with.recommendation: Keep number matching enforced, and block legacy and scripted user agents with Conditional Access.

with.observation: AP rang the supplier on the number in the supplier file before changing anything, which stopped the payment.
with.recommendation: Keep the call-back rule for every bank detail change, whatever the amount.

with.observation: No alert fired on an inbox rule that matched a supplier's domain and moved mail to RSS Subscriptions.
with.recommendation: Alert on new inbox rules that move mail to rarely used folders or mark it read.

record.title: MFA fatigue and consent grants
record.summary: Hypothesis: the actor behind the invoice fraud (#{bec}) tried the same MFA fatigue against other finance users, or got an app consented to read mail (T1621, T1528). Look for bursts of three or more denied pushes followed by an approval, from addresses near 198.51.100.23, and new user consents to multi-tenant apps with Mail.Read or offline_access in the last 30 days. Disproved by: no such bursts outside the AP clerk, and no new consents to unverified publishers.

record.title: Scheduled-task persistence
record.summary: Hypothesis: the Helix affiliate keeps persistence on finance workstations through scheduled tasks that run binaries from user-writable paths (T1053.005), as it did on FIN-WS-0142 in #{rw}. @{team:Intelligence} reports the same pattern from the partner's cases. Look for tasks registered in the last 30 days whose action runs from C:\Users\*, C:\ProgramData or C:\Users\Public, named to look like Microsoft or OneDrive maintenance, and running as SYSTEM. Disproved by: no such task beyond the software inventory's known list.

keys.kt1: Choose data sources and time range
keys.kt4: Conclude: promote it, close it, or refine the hypothesis
keys.kt5: Write up the detection for Shikari's library
keys.kt6: Share what was found with Intelligence

The task name used on FIN-WS-0142.

steps.body: @{team:Intelligence} do the partner's reports give other task names or folders for this affiliate? I'd rather search for the pattern than one name.
Two more names in the partner's reporting: 'EdgeUpdateTaskMachineUA2' and 'OneDriveStandaloneUpdate Task-S-1-5-18', both pointing into C:\Users\Public or C:\ProgramData. Graded B2, as before.

Sources: Defender's DeviceEvents ScheduledTaskCreated (30 days) covers every workstation. Security 4698 isn't collected from workstations, so nothing older than 30 days. @{ana} I'll note that as a visibility gap for Shikari.
